widgets_values:
# Annotate for Edit — the mask pass-through path

**Annotate for Edit**'s default mode is **Pass through**, and in Pass through it never opens Photoshop at all — it just reads whatever you have wired into its **`mask`** input and hands it along, unchanged, alongside your image. This is the plugin-free, ComfyUI-only side of the node.

**Try it:**

1. Queue it as-is. Nothing launches, nothing waits — the node reads the `mask` input (here, a **Solid Mask** standing in for any real mask source) and passes it straight through.
2. Look at the two previews: the image is untouched, and the mask preview shows exactly the gray you set on **Solid Mask** — proof the mask passed through unmodified.
3. Swap **Solid Mask** for any real mask node — an inpaint mask, a segmentation output, hand-painted strokes — and requeue. Anything already in your graph works here.

**No Photoshop, no plugin, no model.** For the Photoshop-driven version of this same node — painting a mask by hand on an Instructions layer — see `annotate-qwen-image-edit.json`, which sets `mode` to *Wait for first save* instead.

nodes.title: Why this demo exists
widgets_values:
# Why this demo exists

This pack's rule is that anything that *can* work without Photoshop, does. **Annotate for Edit** is one of the clearest cases — its default mode needs no plugin and no Photoshop — but until now every demo of this node used the Photoshop path (`mode = Wait for first save`), which made Pass through easy to miss.

**What `mode` does here:** left at its default, **Pass through**. The other two values — *Wait for first save* and *Re-run on every save* — open Photoshop with an editable "Instructions" layer instead; this file deliberately uses neither.

**The `mask` input is optional.** Leave it unconnected and the node hands back an empty mask instead of failing — **Solid Mask** is wired here only to make the pass-through visible in the second preview, not because it's required.

The **`instruction`** and **`annotated`** outputs behave the same in every mode. They are not wired here because this demo is only about the `image` + `mask` pair, but both are available whenever you need them.
